verdicts.trueWording: mostly made up of steep-roofed cottages, separated by twisting streets
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched with a browser UA (HTTP 200). Quote is strict-exact in the arrival read-aloud introduced by 'When the characters arrive in Icehaven, read or paraphrase the following:'. The whole read-aloud names arch, cottages, streets, docks, inn, ship and no inhabitants, so the 'rather than through its inhabitants' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: The following areas in Icehaven are important to this encounter
verdicts.note: Strict-exact, immediately after the arrival read-aloud. Five areas are listed by name (The Haven, The Harborline, Icebreaker Inn and Tavern, House of Warmth, Starosta's Manor) and then appear as numbered sub-headings 1.-5., with cross-references of the form '(area 1)'. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Taskhand Durth Mirimm, the current governor
verdicts.note: Strict-exact in 'The Wastes of Xhorhas and the City of Jigow'. Invented office title (Taskhand) + given name + surname, then the plain-English office in apposition; the sentence goes on to call him the Kryn governor exerting power over local matters.

verdicts.trueWording: a small city by population, but its sprawl of towns
verdicts.note: Strict-exact; full sentence reads 'Jigow is a small city by population, but its sprawl of towns, villages, and neighborhoods stretches across much of the northern coast of Xhorhas.' Both limbs (size label qualified by population; extent given as sprawl) supported.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'ties EACH read-aloud to the precise moment and threshold' - one of the four cues is explicitly left to the DM ('At some point when the characters are in the tavern (at the DM's discretion)'), and a second is tied only to a purpose ('to introduce the characters to some of the bar's other patrons')
verdicts.trueWording: one cue: 'At some point ... at the DM's discretion'
verdicts.note: The quoted cue itself is strict-exact on the page. The article carries four 'Read or paraphrase' cues: the tavern entry (moment), the bar patrons (purpose only), the boasting escalation (explicitly DM discretion, no threshold), and the failure branch (three failures before three successes - a real threshold). So the universal 'each' is not supported; two of four qualify.

verdicts.trueWording: better to simply describe the day's travel in a single sentence
verdicts.note: Strict-exact in the 'Trek to Ten-Towns' travel section; the sentence begins 'if there isn't anything special around' (the unremarkable stretch) and ends 'than to give a litany of uninspired descriptions of a nondescript snowy road'. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: so it doesn't seem like you're reading from a script
verdicts.note: Strict-exact. Full sentence: 'You should improvise a slightly different sentence every time you move from scene to scene, so it doesn't seem like you're reading from a script.' It follows the scene-to-scene read-aloud, so 'vary the wording of a repeated transition' is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: the town's defining feature is [roll the dice] a Sprawling Cemetery
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200, 27KB); byline 'Randy', posted 10/10/2024, covering the Wizards preview with Chris Perkins and interviewer Todd Kenreck. Quote strict-exact; it is the first roll narrated in the demonstration ('[roll the dice]' then 'roll dice again' for claim to fame), which supports the 'first roll' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: What current calamity is befalling the town: Monsters infest the settlement
verdicts.note: Strict-exact in the same settlement demonstration paragraph, third roll in the narrated sequence.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'returning a political condition rather than a person' - the entry's head noun is a leader ('An illegitimate leader'), unnamed but a person-type result, with the condition attached as a participial clause
verdicts.trueWording: Local leaders: An illegitimate leader causing civil unrest
verdicts.note: Quote is strict-exact. The page supports that the result is a leadership situation rather than a named individual, but it does not support the stronger 'a condition rather than a person' framing; the roll returns a leader described by his effect. Downgraded rather than caveated.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'all inside spell and equipment text' - the fourth mention is in the Magic Items chapter's 'Crafting Magic Items' rules (p. 206), a chapter the SRD itself distinguishes from 'Equipment'
verdicts.trueWording: fourth mention sits in 'Crafting Magic Items' (p. 206)
verdicts.note: PDF fetched (HTTP 200, 6.03MB) and text extracted with pdftotext; two extractions agree on exactly four stem occurrences (three 'settlements', one 'settlement'). Locations: p.102 Equipment > Spellcasting services ('Most settlements contain individuals who are willing to cast spells'); p.116 spell Commune with Nature, twice ('castles and settlements'; 'Locations of settlements'); p.206 Magic Items > Crafting Magic Items > Raw Materials ('in any other settlement, that chance is 25 percent'). The 'no settlement-description rules' limb is confirmed: the Gameplay Toolbox lists Travel Pace, Backgrounds, Curses, Environmental Effects, Fear, Poison, Traps and Combat Encounters, and no settlement entry.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'so no lawful open-licence source carries the form' - a universal claim about open-licence sources generally that two documents cannot establish
verdicts.trueWording: zero matches for 'read-aloud' or 'boxed' in both SRDs
verdicts.note: Both PDFs fetched (5.1 HTTP 200, 4.86MB; 5.2.1 HTTP 200, 6.03MB) and extracted with pdftotext. Case-insensitive grep for 'read aloud', 'read-aloud', 'boxed text' and bare 'boxed' returns 0 in each document, so the measured limb is CONFIRMED for both SRDs; only the generalising 'so' clause outruns the evidence.

verdicts.trueWording: The boxed text above serves as a fantastic base
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote strict-exact under 'Arrival in Phandalin' > 'Visual Description'; the passage it points back to is the reprinted Phandalin description, closed by the line 'Source: Dragon of Icespire Peak'. Article bylined Mike Bernier, Sep 18, 2023. Both limbs (reprints the passage; calls it boxed text) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: which consists of forty or fifty simple log buildings
verdicts.note: Strict-exact in the reprinted boxed text sourced to Dragon of Icespire Peak. The passage gives no population figure anywhere - the residents are characterised by trade ('farmers, stonecutters, blacksmiths, traders, prospectors, and children'), never counted - so 'sizes the town by counting its buildings rather than its people' holds.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'rather than as a description' - the same sentence continues 'but most of the adults keep weapons within easy reach in case the need for arms should arise', a positive description of the town's defence
verdicts.trueWording: 'The town has no walls and no garrison' plus armed adults
verdicts.note: Quote is strict-exact and the 'two absences' limb (no walls, no garrison) is fully supported. The contrastive second clause of the same sentence supplies a positive defensive description, so the exclusive framing is downgraded rather than caveated.
